findings.title: Lightness value changed for light theme instead of just adding a dark-theme fallback

The refactor changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The first argument (used for the default/light theme) should have kept the original 30% lightness value (with 70% used for the $secondary/dark branch), but the values were swapped. This means the default light theme's link color changes unintentionally (becomes much lighter, reducing contrast), which is outside the stated scope of this PR (only adding dark-theme support via $secondary).

findings.title: Group member name color lost its distinct lightness value, now identical to title
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, distinguishing it from `.title`'s `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. After the refactor, `.name` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` — identical to `.title`'s new value. The light-theme lightness for `.name` was changed from 30% to 50% instead of being preserved, so the two elements that previously had different visual prominence now render with the same color in the default theme.

findings.title: custom-message-length color values swapped, changing default theme appearance

As a result, the hint text under the custom-message textarea renders much darker/more prominent in the default light theme than it did before this change, which is an unintended visual regression not described by the PR's stated purpose.
